Here is the commit message:
Dispose of DownloadManagerInterface in onDestroy.

This fixes a bug introduced in cf27461bfaa78798252103345b1c14528bb4828c. Prior
to that commit, the DMI was bound to the Application object and there was no
reason to unregister the download receiver. Now that it's bound to the main
activity, there is.

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by the `DownloadManagerInterface` being bound to the `MainActivity` instead of the `Application` object, leading to the failure to unregister the `downloadCompletionReceiver` when the activity was destroyed. This oversight could result in memory leaks and unintended behavior since the receiver would still be active even after the activity was no longer in use.

Here is the patch:
 
+    @Override
+    protected void onDestroy() {
+        super.onDestroy();
+        DownloadManagerInterface.getInstance().destroy(this);
+    }
+
     private void initializeStrictMode() {
         if (BuildConfig.DEBUG) {
             StrictMode.setThreadPolicy(new StrictMode.ThreadPolicy.Builder()
                     .detectAll()
                     .penaltyLog()
                     .penaltyFlashScreen()
                     .penaltyDeathOnNetwork()
                     .build());
 
             StrictMode.setVmPolicy(new StrictMode.VmPolicy.Builder()
                     .detectAll()
                     .penaltyLog()
                     .setClassInstanceLimit(BackendInterface.class, 1)
                     .setClassInstanceLimit(DownloadManagerInterface.class, 1)
                     .build());
         }
     }
 }
